item.title: FSU football eyes fresh start under Rick Stockstill
item.description: When Florida State football plays Boston College at Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill on Saturday, things will look different. Most obviously, the Seminoles (3-5, 1-4 ACC) will be under the direction of a new head coach for the first time in seven seasons, with interim head coach Rick Stockstill wearing the headset once again. The program fired Mike Norvell on Sunday, Nov. 1, after a 36-24 loss to Clemson that featured a mostly empty Doak Campbell Stadium in the fourth quarter and a misspelled plane banner calling for Norvell's removal. The game was labeled as a "defining moment" for university president Richard McCullough, who ultimately relieved Norvell of his duties. It leaves Stockstill with four games to try and avoid a third consecutive losing season for the program, and it starts with the road trip to Boston College. If the Seminoles are going to win a first road game in nearly three years, it might be because of the "subtle" changes that Stockstill said he'd make to the program's game day operation. "There'll be some subtle changes, some little things different... You can't come in and do a lot of wholesale changes schematically, you know, in the ninth week or the 10th week of the season," Stockstill said. "So there will be some changes." Stockstill won't "overload" Ashton Daniels, Tim Harris Jr. calling plays One of the first things Stockstill has to navigate is the change in offensive play caller. While Tim Harris Jr. served as the program's offensive coordinator under Norvell, the former head coach called the plays. Harris is now the play caller, and while his offensive philosophy isn't dissimilar to Norvell's, there will be some alterations. Harris, in his time at UCF, Florida International, and as head coach at Booker. T. Washington had explosive offenses that leaned on the run game. It's similar to Norvell, but pre-snap motions and misdirection might play more of a factor in Harris's offense. With Ashon Daniels under center, the quarterback is a capable fit for Harris. He was initially brought in by Gus Malzahn before his retirement, and Harris's offense won't be far off what Malzahn ran. For Stockstill, the biggest thing he wants to take some stuff off Daniels plate. "He is a strong, powerful runner that can move the sticks for you. I think he does a lot of good things. And to me, we just got to, you know, don't overload him," Stockstill said. "To me, that's the worst thing you can do with a quarterback is put so much on his plate, so many checks that he forgets about something simple over here because he's thinking so much." How that shows up in play calling will be something to monitor. Daniels was used heavily in the run-pass-option (RPO) game under Norvell, and had varied results. Even if Harris continues to put him in those situations, expect a simplified approach to get the ball out of Daniels' hands quicker, or handed off to the runner. item.title: How can Ohio State football beat Oregon? 3 keys to keeping CFP hopes alive
item.description: Here are three keys for No. 12 Ohio State against No. 23 Oregon on Nov. 7: Strike early The Buckeyes should feel a sense of urgency as they look to avoid consecutive regular-season losses for the first time since 2011, a prospect that would leave them needing considerable help to reach the College Football Playoff . After trailing throughout their loss at USC last weekend, they should stress grabbing early momentum rather than being on their heels out of the gate against the Ducks . A fast start would not only leave freshman quarterback Luke Fahey in better spots but also energize the crowd at Ohio Stadium. Ohio State got on the scoreboard first in each of its top-25 wins at Indiana and Iowa in October. Stabilize the back end Dylan Raiola, the former Nebraska quarterback who transferred to Oregon over the offseason, had his best performance against Northwestern in his third start since replacing Dante Moore, who is out for the year due to a concussion. As Raiola threw for 336 yards and three touchdowns, he completed six passes of at least 20 yards, including a 75-yard pass to Dakorien Moore for a key late score. While the Buckeyes have not been vulnerable to big plays through the air for most of 2026, they surrendered passes of 69 and 70 yards at USC as Jayden Maiava averaged 9.7 yards per attempt, matching former Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza for the most against Matt Patricia’s defense. They’ll need to avoid a repeat. Clean up mistakes There was no shortage of self-inflicted wounds for the Buckeyes at USC. They committed a season-high 11 penalties. They stalled on three of four drives in the red zone. They fumbled in opposing territory. The stakes are too high at this point in the year for Ohio State to leave itself in as many difficult situations. Fahey, who protected the ball against the Trojans in his first start, will need to remain as mistake-free as possible against Oregon, which is tied for third in the Big Ten with nine interceptions. The Buckeyes lean on a core of veterans across both sides of the ball and will need them to show their experience as they enter the stretch run. item.description: Analysts and oddsmakers viewed Ohio State and Oregon football as two of the titans of the FBS entering the season and as favorites to win the national championship . But ahead of their matchup, both teams sit outside the College Football Playoff . The Buckeyes suffered their second loss of the season on Oct. 31, losing 30-18 to USC. True freshman quarterback Luke Fahey started in place of Julian Sayin, who is out with an unspecified injury. After the loss, the Buckeyes received a No. 12 ranking in the CFP top 25, the first team outside the projected bracket. Like the Buckeyes, Oregon is also without its original starting quarterback. The Ducks are 5-3, ranked No. 23 with an outside chance of making the 12-team playoff. Read below about Oregon's up-and-down season below. What went wrong with Oregon football this season? Oregon had the fourth-highest preseason odds of winning the national championship at +800, according to BetMGM. Oregon also retained standout defensive linemen Bear Alexander and A'Mauri Washington and acquired veteran Minnesota safety Koi Perich and UNC defensive tackle D'Antre Robinson in the transfer portal. After beating Portland State 84-0 in Week 3, the Ducks faced USC at home. item.title: 'Hard yards' and a Prague summit
item.description: [Getty Images] For many Bournemouth followers, "doing the hard yards" meant following the team in their League Two days, spending every other Saturday heading to cold northern outposts such as Bury or Rochdale, or further still, Carlisle or Hartlepool. On Thursday evening, hundreds of Cherries fans who had made the journey to Prague and had gathered in the Old Town Square, embarked on the traditional European "fan walk" to the stadium. Having crossed the river still in good spirits, the steep walk up more than a dozen flights of steps into Letna Park dampened that enthusiasm slightly, with some comparing it to the gargantuan climb up into the gods to reach the away end at Newcastle United's St James' Park. The "hard yards" were not yet over, as with Sparta Prague's Epet Arena in sight, supporters were held up by police, and then seemingly directed away from the stadium and down residential streets before finally reaching the away fans' section on the far side of the ground, with kick-off fast approaching. It did not look like it would be Bournemouth's night after Lewis Cook missed a penalty and Sparta took a 1-0 half-time lead to end the Cherries' run of six clean sheets. Cook is not known for his goalscoring prowess, with a record of four goals in 318 appearances across his 10-year Bournemouth career. In his defence, the Cherries' two regular penalty-takers, Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier, were on the substitutes' bench at the time, while Cook did have a perfect three-from-three record in penalty shootouts, netting against Norwich in 2022, Wolves in 2025 and Newcastle earlier this year. Despite having made eight changes for the Sparta game, boss Marco Rose was not to be denied, and was again vindicated in his choice of substitutions as Tyler Adams, Evanilson and Rayan all came off the bench to score in a 3-1 win. So, those who had done the "hard yards" were rewarded with a seventh successive win in all competitions and a continued 100% record in the Europa League. Although some, understandably, took a more leisurely tram ride back to the city centre. Explore Bournemouth content on BBC Sounds

FAMU aims to halt a three-game losing streak , most recently falling to Southern 42-14 last Saturday, Oct. 31, in a Halloween SWAC game. All-time, FAMU is 5-7 against Alcorn State dating back to 1935, according to College Football Results . The Rattlers hosted homecoming and beat the Braves 33-28 last season. Saturday is a homecoming for FAMU head coach Quinn Fordham Gray Sr. , who was Alcorn’s quarterback coach from 2020 to 2022 . item.title: Six police cars descend on Newcastle defender Amar Dedic after star is spotted with bow and arrow at local beauty spot
item.description: Newcastle United v AFC Bournemouth - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Newcastle United summer signing Amar Dedic has found himself at the centre of an unusual police investigation after being spotted with a bow and arrows. The Bosnia and Herzegovina international was reportedly stopped by multiple police cars following concerns raised by a member of the public near a local beauty spot. Armed police swoop on Magpies defender The incident unfolded on Wednesday afternoon when the 24-year-old and a companion were seen walking near a countryside reservoir in the Harlow Hill area. A concerned member of the public contacted the authorities after spotting the pair carrying archery equipment. According to the Daily Mail , six squad cars intercepted Dedic's vehicle in the Darras Hall estate, roughly seven miles from the initial sighting. Officers questioned the Bosnia and Herzegovina international at the scene before confiscating the items. Police confirm seizure of recreational weapons Authorities were quick to ease any major public safety concerns regarding the ordeal. A spokesperson for Northumbria Police confirmed that officers responded swiftly to the afternoon sighting. "Shortly after 1.55pm (Wednesday), we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area," the spokesperson stated. They went on to clarify that the situation was safely resolved and posed no broader danger to the community. "Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows," the statement continued. "At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing." Bizarre coincidence as team-mates pass by In a strange twist of fate during the roadside stop, two familiar faces happened to drive past the unfolding scene. The report added that Newcastle backup goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived by pure chance while officers were speaking with their colleague, pulling over to offer assistance. The strange episode caps off an eventful few months for Dedic. The defender only arrived at St James' Park during the recent summer transfer window, completing a £30 million switch from Portuguese giants Benfica. It remains unknown exactly what the duo intended to use the sporting weapons for prior to the police intervention. Turning focus back to Premier League duties Despite the police involvement and ongoing enquiries, Dedic remains fully available for selection. Matthias Jaissle's squad will travel to the capital this Saturday afternoon for a crucial Premier League clash against Fulham. The Magpies desperately need a positive result at Craven Cottage to reverse a worrying slump in form. Newcastle have suffered four defeats in their last five outings, placing immense pressure on the team to secure three points in west London.

item.title: Florida State's search should start with Stein, Dillingham, Dickert
item.description: A sitting head coach with experience … but not too much experience. That should be Florida State’s plan of pursuit to replace Mike Norvell , who was mercifully fired on Nov. 1 and sent packing with memories of 2023 (13-1 record) and a $50 million buyout. The Seminoles, despite eight years of at least five losses in the last decade (!), are a big boy program playing in a talent-rich state. It is not the job for a first-time coach facing a significant rebuild. Experience in the hot seat should be a pre-requisite. But Seminoles fans should also want somebody who can be a long-term answer. Brian Kelly , 65, wants the job. Jimbo Fisher , 61, would take the job for the federal minimum wage. No thanks. The Seminoles’ search , once they hire an athletic director (which should be done first), should start with three names. I would call Kentucky’s Will Stein just to make sure he says no. If he’s interested in leaving the Wildcats after one year, every single resource should be devoted to pursuing him. Yes, he just has the single season as a big whistle, but he’s worth it. If Stein isn’t in play, my next two calls would be to Kenny Dillingham at Arizona State and Jake Dickert at Wake Forest. Dillingham, 36, is 26-21 for the Sun Devils and was an FSU assistant in 2020-21 and before that, was at Auburn for one year. Arizona State is 4-4 this year. Dickert, 43, has won at Washington State and Wake Forest. Think about that. He was 23-20 at Washington State and 14-5 at Wake (only loss this year is to Miami). A big leap from Winston-Salem to Tallahassee? Yes, but I want a guy who has turned programs around. That’s my list: 1. Stein; 2. Dillingham; 3. Dickert. Jaguars big road favorite Twelve hours before the Jacksonville Jaguars - Baltimore Ravens kickoff on Nov. 5, the sharps had bet the Jaguars to a 10-point favorite (they opened at minus-8) because the Ravens lost quarterbacks Lamar Jackson (right thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the season in their Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills . Suffice it to say, being a double-digit road favorite is rare territory for the Jaguars. If the line held at minus-10, it would have marked the first time since Dec. 17, 2000, at Cincinnati when the Jaguars were minus-10 1/2 and lost 17-14. Before the Ravens game, the Jaguars were 4-1 straight-up all-time when a double-digit road favorite and 2-3 against the spread. The largest spread? They were a 14 1/2-point favorite at Cleveland on Dec. 19, 1999, and won 24-14. item.title: Hockey’s streaming spree means there’s one fewer thing holding Canada together
item.description: Connor McDavid is in a rich vein of form for the Oilers. Photograph: Pamela Smith/AP The Oilers lost to the Detroit Red Wings on 26 October, but Edmonton captain Connor McDavid got an assist anyway. He’s been doing that a lot lately. Just 16 games into the year, McDavid has 31 assists. It’s the fastest anyone has ever hit that milestone in any NHL season. But on that night in late October, many fans in Edmonton were unable to see McDavid’s feats – including patrons of a local bar – because it was one of nine Oilers games this season that are only available via a subscription to a premium streaming service. It’s the same story in every Canadian NHL city, thanks to changes to broadcasts that have meant that a handful of games for each team are now only available with a $12.99 per month subscription to Sportsnet+, a streaming channel owned by Canadian telecom juggernaut – and owner of the Toronto Maple Leafs – Rogers Communications Inc. But it’s not just Sportsnet+. The NHL also expanded its broadcast deal with Amazon, so when, two nights after the game against Detroit, the Oilers played their provincial rival, the Calgary Flames, only Amazon Prime subscribers could watch (true to form, McDavid got two assists in that one). It gets worse. In June, the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation, Canada’s public broadcaster, announced it would stop airing Saturday night games – Hockey Night in Canada – for the first time since 1952. Again, Rogers played a role. In 2013, the telecom company signed a $5.2bn deal with the NHL for the league’s Canadian rights, with a sublicensing deal with the CBC to jointly present Saturday games. When the two sides couldn’t reach a new agreement, Rogers went ahead alone on its 12-year, $11bn rights renewal that started in October. “Watching hockey on Saturday night is a time-honoured tradition for Canadians, and Sportsnet is privileged to continue delivering that tradition,” the network said in a statement when the split was announced. Needless to say, “delivering” was doing a lot of work in that sentence, and no surprise, Canadians hate the arrangement now that they see what it means. Data released last week from Canadian pollster Angus Reid shows that 78% of Canadians say that “it’s bad that more games require additional subscriptions” and 63% say they pay too much for Sportsnet+, while roughly a third (33%) say Amazon Prime is too expensive. Hardly surprising, when the cost of living remains atop the list of issues facing Canadians. An even higher proportion (79%) say that it’s become too expensive overall to follow their favourite NHL team. Having an experienced starter at quarterback is key for any college football program to achieve success. One way to do just that is by getting signal-callers from the transfer portal. Perhaps the school that's been most successful in doing so is the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes . For the past three straight seasons, Canes head coach Mario Cristobal has landed three big-time transfer quarterbacks. His first was former Washington State signal-caller Cam Ward in 2024. Last season, he turned to former Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Carson Beck. He helped lead Miami to its first-ever national title game since the 2001-02 season. 2026 might be Cristobal's most effective transfer quarterback yet, as he landed Darian Mensah from Duke. Although Ward had previously declared for the 2024 NFL Draft, he did not hire an agent and was thus still eligible to play in college. item.description: Te’Yala Delfosse and the Michigan Wolverines. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The downside of decades of dominance? It’s only news when you lose. On Thursday night in Ann Arbor, No. 2 UConn lost to No. 5 Michigan, 77-66. As Michigan head coach Kim Barnes Arico said after the game , “How many teams beat UConn? It doesn’t happen.” The loss snapped the Huskies’ 39-game regular-season winning streak, all while sinking the prospects of another undefeated UConn campaign after just two games. Yet, UConn never beats themselves, thus demanding that Michigan receive requisite praise, and then some, for earning the highest-ranked win in program history. A 22-13 was the finishing flourish in the fourth quarter—in short, out-executing the Huskies in winning time—secured the win for the Wolverines. The Wolverine win also might have berth women’s college basketball’s newest star: Te’Yala Delfosse. Te'Yala Delfosse (11/5/26) pic.twitter.com/ghG6vb5Nhh — @balapattyszn (@balapattyvids) November 6, 2026 The 6-foot-3 junior forward led Michigan with a career-high 22 points, showing off an intriguing combination of athleticism and skill as she helped the Wolverines puncture a usually-stout Husky defense. A 32 percent 3-point shooter across her first two college seasons, Delfosse went 3-for-4 from downtown, demonstrating a quick, comfortable release on her catch-and-shoot conversions. She paired that shooting with assertive attacks to the basket, using her long strides, solid handle and finishing touch both in transition and halfcourt situations. She also added nine rebounds, two steals and a block. item.description: Jurgen Klopp confirms on-loan Barcelona veteran will be Germany’s number 1: ‘He has the most experience’ Marc Andre ter Stegen has received an important boost to his international career after Germany manager Jurgen Klopp confirmed that the Barcelona goalkeeper will be his first choice for the upcoming fixtures. Currently on loan at Ajax, the 34-year-old has gradually rebuilt his confidence in the Netherlands after a difficult period at Barcelona, with his improved performances helping him regain prominence in the national team setup. Ter Stegen’s situation has changed considerably following a campaign disrupted by injuries and inconsistent performances. After missing out on the World Cup because of a physical setback, the German is now enjoying regular football under Michel and has regained the confidence of the national team management. Ajax spell helps Ter Stegen rebuild his confidence The move to Ajax has provided Ter Stegen with an opportunity to rediscover the consistency that previously made him one of Europe’s most respected goalkeepers. Marc-Andre ter Stegen will be Germany’s number 1. Although his performances in Amsterdam have included occasional mistakes, the most encouraging development has been his ability to maintain regular involvement without the recurring physical problems that disrupted his previous campaign. For a goalkeeper whose confidence and match rhythm are closely connected to regular appearances, finding an environment where he feels important again has been quite valuable. Klopp confirms Ter Stegen as Germany’s first-choice goalkeeper Ter Stegen’s improved situation has now been recognised by Klopp, who has confirmed that the Barcelona-owned goalkeeper will start Germany’s upcoming matches. item.title: LSU women’s basketball sets D1 victory margin record
item.description: Do not adjust your screens for the following information: on Thursday, the #9 LSU women’s basketball team beat Texas Southern 131-22 in a game that set several records. The 109-point margin of victory is the largest in a D1 vs D1 game, breaking the previous record set on December 15, 2016, by Kim Mulkey’s Baylor team in a 140-32 clobbering of Winthrop. The Bayou Barbie got to see a thorough beatdown. How it happened Texas Southern played things relatively close in the first quarter and only trailed 25-13. The SWAC Tigers took two early leads on uncontested threes before LSU started turning them over and getting a bit of a groove going. The second quarter was a 40-0 bloodbath that set an NCAA record for most points in a shutout quarter in a D1 vs D1 game and second most behind Texas Southern’s 44-0 first quarter in a November 26, 2024, game against the College of Biblical Studies (an NCCAA school in Houston that I can confirm is real based on going to two games they played). TSU couldn’t hit a shot to save their lives or keep from losing the ball. At the half, LSU led 65-13. LSU finished off the 50-0 run in the third before TSU hit a relieving three, the only shot they’d hit in the quarter. LSU won the quarter 30-3. The fourth quarter was yet more LSU dominance and ended 36-6. The SEC Tigers’ starters had to play several minutes to give the reserves some rest, but it was the bench who came in and finished the job. Two Meghan Yarnevich free throws brought the lead from 107 to 109 and capped off a record-setting night. Team stats LSU shot 60% on 53/89 shooting, and the 53 made shots set a new program record for field goals in a game. item.description: Jarrod Bowen West Ham 2026-27 goal - Getty Bowen married into the West Ham-mad Dyer family After being left out of Thomas Tuchel’s 2026 World Cup plans, to the surprise of many, Bowen opted to ignore any exit talk during the summer transfer window . Instead, he agreed to revised terms at the London Stadium. He vowed to help the Hammers bounce back into the big time at the first attempt. Family ties - having married into the Dyer family when tying the knot with Strictly Come Dancing contestant and former Love Island star Dani - made it difficult to consider a new challenge. Talented forward opted to ignore any transfer rumours Talented forward opted to ignore any transfer rumours The 29-year-old winger is tied to a contract with West Ham through to 2030 and had been hoping to play his way towards retirement on their books. He has already taken in close to 300 appearances for the club and become a talismanic presence with 94 goals to his name. item.title: Didier Deschamps to Real Madrid? How Jose Mourinho beat the former France boss to the Santiago Bernabeu hotseat
item.description: DIDIER DESCHAMPS FRANCE - Getty Images Didier Deschamps was eager to become the new Real Madrid manager this summer before the Spanish club opted to appoint Jose Mourinho instead. The former France boss is now assessing his options amid reported interest from struggling Manchester United and Juventus. Missing out on the Madrid job Deschamps ended his remarkable 14-year tenure as France manager in July following a thrilling 6-4 defeat to England in the World Cup third-place play-off. The 58-year-old is currently resting as he waits for an exciting new challenge to emerge. However, the World Cup winner could have returned to management almost immediately. According to Foot Mercato , Deschamps was highly interested in taking charge at Real Madrid. He wanted to replace Alvaro Arbeloa in the Spanish capital following the conclusion of the World Cup. Ultimately, Los Blancos decided to appoint Mourinho instead. A perfect environment in the Spanish capital Madrid would have represented an ideal destination for Deschamps due to the immense prestige of the club. It would have also offered a familiar environment for the French tactician. Deschamps already speaks fluent Spanish, having spent a year playing for Valencia during the 2000-01 season. Furthermore, the move would have reunited him with several of his former international players. The current Real Madrid squad boasts a strong French contingent. Deschamps would have linked up with Kylian Mbappe, Eduardo Camavinga, Aurelien Tchouameni, Ferland Mendy and Ibrahima Konate at the Santiago Bernabeu. Manchester United make contact over vacancy Despite missing out on the Madrid role, the former France boss remains a highly sought-after figure in the managerial market. The same reports claims that United have already contacted Deschamps to request information about his availability. The Premier League club are actively exploring the market as current manager Michael Carrick remains under immense pressure at Old Trafford. The Red Devils view the experienced Frenchman as a potential solution to their ongoing struggles. However, Deschamps is reportedly unenthusiastic about the prospect of moving to northern England. The 58-year-old is willing to listen to offers but is not rushing into his next managerial position. Waiting for the right European opportunity Deschamps is prepared to be patient as he weighs up his options for the future. The veteran coach could even wait until next summer before officially resuming his managerial career. Alongside United, Deschamps has also been strongly linked with Juventus in recent days. The Italian club are reportedly considering parting ways with head coach Luciano Spalletti in the near future. For now, Deschamps will continue to monitor the landscape across Europe's top leagues. He remains in a strong position to secure a high-profile job when the right opportunity finally presents itself.

item.title: Bill Simmons proxy betting case lands FanDuel in major Massachusetts hearing
item.description: Bill Simmons’ offhand podcast story about letting his daughter’s boyfriend bet for him has turned into a formal Massachusetts Gaming Commission case, and FanDuel is the company that will have to answer for it. Commissioners voted Thursday unanimously to hold an adjudicatory hearing with the sportsbook after enforcement staff reported that 22 wagers totaling $21,800 were placed through Simmons’ account on Aug. 5, Aug. 7 and Aug. 19. A hearing date hasn’t been set. MORE: Week 10 college football best bets: Ohio State, Oklahoma face pivotal tests What Bill Simmons admitted on his podcast Former ESPN personality and founder of The Ringer Bill Simmons The Ringer founder told the story during an Aug. 30 episode of The Bill Simmons Podcast while picking AFC win totals. He was in California, where sports betting isn’t legal, and wanted money down on UCLA and Houston Texans futures through his Massachusetts FanDuel account. So he turned to Hank, his daughter’s 21-year-old boyfriend in Massachusetts, and gave him the verification code sent to his phone. “I let Hank log into my FanDuel as me,” Simmons said. “A week later, called him up and ran it back. We did some more.” The state’s sports wagering law requires operators to stop anyone from betting as a proxy for someone else. FanDuel, The Ringer’s exclusive betting partner, reported the matter to regulators the next day, voided the bets and took unspecified action on the account. Commissioner Paul Brodeur asked whether action against Simmons or the bettor remained possible. item.title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Crew Offered $3,000 Hazard Pay To Travel To Saudi Arabia (WWE News)
item.description: WWE WrestleVotes on Fightful Select has heard from in-house sources that "several crew members have opted out of making the trip" to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia for WWE 's Crown Jewel PLE on 7 November. In addition, the company " is offering crew members additional hazard pay for making the trip". Even more interestingly, this isn't anywhere close to the norm - WWE/TKO don't typically need to offer danger pay, but events in Saudi have people (rightly) spooked. Those staffers electing not to go spurned "additional compensation" to fly out. WrestleVotes spoke about this with 2 people working for WWE . They revealed that the hazard pay sits at $3,000. According to Fightful's write up, " Hazard pay is additional pay for performing hazardous duty or work involving physical hardship. Work duty that causes extreme physical discomfort and distress which is not adequately alleviated by protective devices is deemed to impose a physical hardship". Crown Jewel has been dangling by a thread for a while now . Internally, concurrent reports suggested that WWE/TKO even considered moving the event entirely, but things have been a little cloudy on that front in terms of definitive news. This wasn't included in the WrestleVotes/Fightful story, but it'd be a surprise if the promotion didn't have a backup venue in mind domestically. After all, they've known about the tensions/trouble in Saudi Arabia for ages. The show will go ahead in Riyadh as planned , but not everyone working for WWE is comfortable with going there and producing the event. $3,000 add-ons haven't cut it for some.
